title: Handoff Snowball: Canary Patterns & Steward Rituals (wip)
body:
Purpose and scope

This is a working sketch of a cross-functional lightweight playbook we can use for small-to-medium surfaced feature rollouts where model behavior, latency and cost interact (examples: new reranker model, multi-model routing change, embedding-upgrade). The emphasis is on a compact steward ritual and an automated safety net we can hand off to on-call and product owners. Not a canonical enterprise spec — practical, executable, and intentionally terse.

Core idea (the "snowball")

- Start small, check early signals, and expand exposure by doubling cohorts instead of linear additions.
- Each expansion is gated by explicit metric checks (safety + business) and a one-line human confirmation from the steward.
- Keep fallbacks ready (model-variant mapping, region failover, capacity tier) so expansion is a single operator action (flip route/scale) and reversion is automated.

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners)

- Steward: owner for the rollout day. Confirms gates, runs manual checks, triggers expansion or rollback. (Primary: PM / Product-Owner)
- Observability lead: exposes dashboards and pushes thresholds into Redwood Console. (Primary: Eng-observability)
- Runtime owner: rollback and capacity actions (Primary: Serving-runtime or Platform-eng)
- On-call: executes emergency cutover per incident runbook (Primary: SRE)
- Data science / Eval: monitors quality regressions and signal drift (Primary: Applied-ML)

Initial checklist (pre-activation)

- [ ] Canary implementation: route 1% (or single microcohort) to new model/behavior, rest to baseline.
- [ ] Guardrail dashboard: latency P50/P95, token-cost per request, error-rate, and two quality proxies (synthetic prompt scoring, user-reported rate).
- [ ] Synthetic probe harness: 200 fixed prompts + 100 wildcard queries run at 3am and 11am to detect nondeterministic failures.
- [ ] Instrument cost leaks: per-token cost alert (monthly burn estimate) and per-request token delta for the route.
- [ ] Fallback mapping table committed: model -> variant -> fallback route (e.g., gen-v2 -> gen-v1-quantized -> pinned smaller model).
- [ ] Stakeholder announce: #launch-room Slack channel, 1-line brief + steward assignment.

Steward ritual (day-of)

- T-30m: checklist + confirm traces linked in Redwood Console. Quick smoke: 10 human review prompts.
- Activate 1% microcohort. Post-stable-warmup wait: 5–10m depending on model warm-up behavior.
- Run synthetic probe battery (should be automated).
- Evaluate gates. If all clear, steward responds in Slack with: "GO-EXPAND: step=1 justification=<short note>"
- Expand cadence: double exposure every 30–60m for latency-sensitive features, every 2–4h for riskier behavioral changes.

Safety gates (example thresholds)

- Hard (auto-rollback): error-rate increase > 300% OR absolute error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m; latency P95 increase > 300ms vs baseline for 10m; token-cost per request > 150% of baseline for sustained 30m.
- Soft (steward decision): synthetic quality score drop > 5 points (out of 100) OR user-reported negative feedback rate > 0.2% in cohort for 1h.
- Statistical note: for small cohorts use exact binomial checks; for expansions beyond 5% treat metrics with sequential testing (alpha spending). Data-science should provide quick p-values on steward request.

A/B evaluation window and metrics prioritization

- Primary metrics: latency P95 (user-facing), cost per request, and a domain-specific quality proxy (e.g., normalized rerank NDCG or hallucination score).
- Secondary: engagement uplift (% users using new feature), completion rate, follow-on API calls (downstream token usage).
- Window guidance: quick signal (hours) for latency/cost; quality needs longer (3–7 days) depending on sparsity. If the business metric is conversion, budget a 2–4 week test.

Cohort sizing & selection patterns

- Microcohort (1%): random bucket, but prefer high-traffic stable pages rather than low-volume fringe segments. Avoid cohorts with known cold-start behavior.
- Snowball doubling: 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8% -> 16% -> 32% (stop if any gate trips).
- Biased cohort option: test on internal staff / power-users first (canary-in-team) for behavioral regressions before public cohorts.

Common failure modes & countermeasures

- Oscillation (flip-flop): introduce a minimum cool-down (30m) between adjustments and prefer stepwise reduction if instability seen.
- Cost shock after expansion: automatic rate-limiter that caps the new route's throughput to a predicted spend-change ceiling; steward override with justification.
- Model warm-up causing transient latency spike: mark initial expansion windows as warm-up and ignore first 15m for latency gate (but not for errors).
- Silent quality drift: schedule periodic manual sample review (10 random outputs every 6h) and add synthetic probes targeting edge cases.

Runbook snippets (copy-paste friendly)

- Slack launch message template:
  LAUNCH ROOM: Activating snowball for <feature> on <date/time>. Steward: <name>. Initial exposure: 1% (bucket A). Dashboards: <url>. If any hard gate triggers, SRE will cut traffic to baseline within 2m.

- Emergency rollback command (ops):
  /rollout route set <route-name> --target baseline --force --reason "auto-rollback or steward stop"

- Quick steward checklist (one-liner per item):
  [ ] dashboard up, [ ] synthetic probes green, [ ] smoke prompts passed, [ ] communicate to launch room, [ ] expand?

Experiment tagging & observability implementation details

- Tag all requests with header X-Rollout-ID and X-Cohort, surface in traces. Redwood Console should allow slice-by X-Rollout-ID.
- Push aggregated metrics into the release-specific dashboard: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, cost-per-request, synthetic-probe score, user-feedback rate.
- Keep a running CSV in the release folder with raw cohort counts and outcome counts for simple postmortems.

Open questions / TODOs

- How do we integrate sequential statistical testing into Console so stewards get instant p-values? (Action: ask Applied-ML for a minimal estimator).
- What default cool-downs make sense for high-throughput vs low-throughput features? (Action: SRE to propose template).
- Enable an automated canary that will escalate to on-call if a hard-gate trips outside business hours. (Action: Platform-eng)

Appendix: short example (reranker swap)

Scenario: swap reranker model from rerank-v1 to rerank-v2 that improves NDCG but is 20% slower and 10% more tokens.

- Pre-steps: synthetic rerank test suite (100 items) -> v2 median NDCG +4.5 points.
- Canary: 1% traffic, synthetic probes every 30m, cost alert set to +12% delta.
- Gates: soft for synthetic NDCG drop >2.5 points, hard for P95 latency +200ms.
- Expansion cadence: 1% -> 2% (30m) -> 4% (1h) -> 8% (2h) -> 16% (4h). Pause at any steward note.
- Fallback: immediate route to rerank-v1. If cost growth persists at 16% exposure, revert the change and open an incident to optimize quantization/kv caching.

Notes to self

- Keep this short and iteratively add templates: Slack snippets, API rollback commands, and a minimal statistical helper script.
- Share with Solutions Eng and SRE for feedback before wider adoption.

Unresolved: final wording for the auto-rollback thresholds — more conservative for premium customers and dedicated deployments (because cost vs SLA tradeoffs differ).

End of draft.
